g.text: about 10 years over continuing smokers, and quitting at 60 about 3. US adults showed a similar pattern.

g.text: DATA Doll et al., BMJ 328:1519 (2004); Jha et al., NEJM 368:341 (2013); Pirie et al., Lancet 381:133 (2013).

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono'; fill: #8c877d

g.text: Values transcribed from the papers' text. Excess risk avoided = 1 - (RR ex-smoker - 1) / (RR still smoking - 1).

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono'; fill: #8c877d

g.text: *Derived here; the paper says at least two-thirds.

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono'; fill: #8c877d

g.text: NOTE Cohort comparisons adjusted for age and other factors, not trials. People who quit can differ from those who don't.
